prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Transport Through Time; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: A selected past-to-present comparison of transport power followed by clearly supervised prototypes for future use. Historical pictures are reconstructions, not one universal worldwide timeline. Plain practical clothing and neutral locations only; no flags, religious/political symbols, brands or named child cast. Past examples: a bay horse with brown wooden wagon, a wooden rowing boat and cream-sailed wooden boat, black steam locomotive with red wheels and brown coaches, early dark-green motor car, blue motor bus and red goods truck, cream propeller biplane. Present examples: white passenger ferry, blue-hulled container ship, white-and-teal passenger jet, white-and-blue electric train, blue battery car, teal electric bus, blue pedal-assist bicycle and orange cargo bicycle. Prototypes: white car with teal trim and mounted camera/roof sensor on closed test track; white-and-orange small electric propeller aircraft in a test hangar. Prototypes have adult supervision; their illustration is not a forecast that this exact design will be adopted.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Bay horse and brown wooden wagon; Wooden rowing boat with two coherent oars; Small wooden sailing boat with cream sail; Black steam locomotive with red wheels and two brown coaches; Early dark-green car, blue bus and red goods truck; White passenger ferry and blue-hulled container ship; Cream biplane and white teal-tail passenger jet; White-blue electric train, blue battery car and teal electric bus; Blue electric bicycle and orange cargo bicycle with empty child seat; White teal-trim camera-and-sensor test car; White-orange small experimental electric propeller aircraft; Closed battery modules, workshop scale, trolley and chargers
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 9. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): Engineers also test electric aircraft. Lighter batteries could help these planes carry more people farther before they need to charge.
Required illustration: A small white-and-orange experimental electric propeller aircraft stands completely on its landing gear at a test hangar. One nose-mounted electric motor and propeller, one fuselage, a correctly attached pair of wings and one tail are coherent and fully framed. An adult engineer in plain work clothes weighs one compact rectangular battery module on a low workshop scale beside the parked plane; a second closed matching battery module rests on a trolley. A charging cable is connected to the aircraft on the other side, clear of the propellers and walking area. This is a plausible test aircraft, not a guaranteed future airliner or a vehicle already carrying crowds. No labels, digits, logos or open unsafe electrical parts.
Exact current state: Experimental electric flight introduces battery weight as a design constraint. Lighter suitable batteries could improve payload/range; no date or inevitable adoption is promised.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
Render 1536 by 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2. Clean crisp 2D cartoon, no embossed or painted texture. Keep all required subjects fully inside an 8 percent safe margin, with coherent human anatomy and vehicle geometry. This is a finished individual book illustration: never reproduce the reference board or add unrequested subjects/panels. No words, numbers, logos, flags, title or watermark. If several panels are authored, each contains only its exact requested vehicle scene. Future examples are supervised tests, not a claim that they are available for ordinary passenger use.

visualReview.note: One white/orange experimental plane with a single nose-mounted electricpropeller stands on its landing gear at a hangar. Both wings/tail attach coherently. Engineer places one closed battery module on a scale; another rests on a trolley; charging cable attaches to the plane clear of its propeller. The scene concretely shows battery testing, not a guaranteed future airliner carrying public passengers.
